blocks.markdown: Policy, creation, and the duty to insure — objectives: state the Sec. 2 State policy, explain PDIC's creation and Board, and apply the mandatory insurance duty (Sec. 6) and bank assessments (Sec. 7).
PDIC is a **statutory, mandatory deposit insurer**: Congress created it, every deposit-taking bank must belong, and the twin mission is **protecting depositors plus stabilizing banking**.

Think of PDIC as the banking system's safety net with three non-obvious features. **First, coverage is automatic**: a depositor never applies and never pays a premium — insurance attaches the moment money is deposited in an insured bank. **Second, the banks pay**: PDIC is funded by semi-annual assessments levied on banks (a bank operating expense), not by depositors. **Third, PDIC wears two hats**: insurer that pays depositors when a bank closes, and receiver-liquidator that takes over and winds up the closed bank. Since RA 11840 (2022) it is attached to the BSP for policy coordination while keeping fiscal and administrative autonomy.
Memorize the three limbs: **(1) MANDATORY system**, **(2) faith-and-confidence purpose** (plus protection against illegal schemes), **(3) PDIC autonomy**.

Why examiners love Sec. 2: it justifies everything drastic PDIC does. A bank run is a confidence failure, so the State answers with **permanent, continuing, mandatory** coverage — 'permanent and continuing' means protection does not lapse or need renewal. The 'illegal schemes and machinations' clause is the policy anchor for denying fictitious, fraudulent, and money-laundering deposits later in this module. And the autonomy clause explains PDIC's speed: takeover, payout, and liquidation decisions do not wait for other agencies. **Remember**: when a problem asks WHY deposit insurance exists or why it is compulsory, answer with Sec. 2 first, then the facts.
Seven members, four votes to act: **BSP Governor (Chair) + Finance Secretary (Vice-Chair) + PDIC President + 4 private-sector directors** (6-year terms, one reappointment).

Count '1-1-1-4': one BSP Governor, one Finance Secretary, one PDIC President, four appointive private-sector directors — seven total, all drawn through the GOCC Governance Commission shortlist process (RA 10149). Quorum and decision rule is **four**. Practical memory hook: the Board holds every money lever in the charter — it sets the **assessment rate**, **raises the MDIC** (as it did in 2025), approves the DIF target, and directs receivership and liquidation. Any problem citing a 'five-member Board' or a Finance-Secretary chair is using pre-2022 law.
The duty sentence is absolute — **'shall be insured'** — and the 2022 amendment adds Islamic-banking windows plus early-warning risk evaluation of capital-deficient banks.

Two applications. **Depositor scenario**: Gina opens a savings account in a rural bank and asks whether she must enroll in PDIC — answer: no enrollment, no premium; Sec. 6 insures the bank's deposit liabilities by operation of law, and Gina is covered up to the MDIC automatically. **Bank-accounting angle**: the same section is why assessments are an unavoidable bank operating cost — a bank cannot resign from insurance while it takes deposits, and its full GROSS deposit liabilities enter the assessment base (Sec. 7). The 2022 risk-evaluation paragraph matters before failure: once BSP flags capital deficiency, PDIC may value the bank's assets and classify its risk to shield the DIF — prevention, not yet closure.
Funding formula: Board-set rate capped at **1/5 of 1% p.a.**, semi-annual payment on **gross** deposit liabilities, **P5,000 floor** — plus Board power to adjust the rate when the MDIC rises.

Illustration at the ceiling rate (hypothetical — the Board sets the actual rate within the cap): a bank with P10 billion in deposit liabilities pays at most 1/5 of 1% per year, or P20 million annually — P10 million per semester — with no deduction for borrowers' unpaid loans. Two traps: **(1)** the base is gross liabilities — netting loans is disallowed; **(2)** depositors never shoulder assessments, so a problem charging depositors a 'PDIC premium' states an error of law. The MDIC-link sentence is the 2025 story: higher coverage justified the Board's review of whether rates keep the DIF adequate and sustainable.
Three powers carry this module: **examine** (even through secrecy walls on fraud/unsafe-banking findings), **act as receiver** (every closed bank), and **choose and run the liquidation mode**.

blocks.markdown: **Trap: pre-2022 materials are wrong on four points.** (1) Section numbers moved in 2016 — old Sec. 4(f) is now Sec. 5(g), old Sec. 4(g) is Sec. 5(k), old Sec. 22 (TRO ban) is Sec. 27. (2) The Board has 7 members chaired by the BSP Governor, not 5 chaired by Finance. (3) The MDIC is P1M since 15 March 2025, not P500,000. (4) Splitting's window is 120 days, not 30. Always restate old citations in current numbering.

**Answer formula for PDIC policy problems:** (1) cite the charter section in CURRENT numbering; (2) quote or closely track the statutory sentence; (3) apply each element to the facts (who acts, what triggers, what limits); (4) state the dated figure with its issuance (e.g., 'P1M MDIC, Memo 2025-01, eff. 15 Mar 2025'); (5) close with the consequence (coverage, denial, remedy, penalty). Never cite the syllabus or a textbook as authority.
